newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU explains itself to aspiring new members.
newsitem.headline: EU explains itself to aspiring new members.

text.p: The European Union met leaders from 12 aspirant countries on Friday to explain the state of the bloc after its recent summit which agreed a new treaty.

Among one of the key messages the bloc was expected to deliver to the candidates, all eager to cross the threshold early next century, was that key internal EU reforms necessary to prepare it for eastwards expansion have not yet been achieved.

Leaders from 10 eastern European candidates for EU entry -- Poland, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Slovakia, Slovenia, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Romania and Bulgaria -- were at the meeting, along with those from Cyprus and Turkey.

Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok and European Commission President Jacques Santer were set to debrief the 12 on the outcome of the EU's June 16-17 Amsterdam summit, after voicing concern on Thursday about the negative impact of the meeting on the EU's eastwards expansion plans.

The summit meeting failed to agree the institutional changes necessary to prevent paralysis in its decision-making when the EU takes on up to a dozen new members and agreed that only when these changes have been agreed can the expansion take place.
The meeting takes places as the eastern European countries nervously await the European Commission's assessment on July 16 of how suitable each of them is for the rigours of EU membership.
Talks with Cyprus, which has already been judged to fit the bill, are due to start early next year.
Turkey's EU application has been shunned on human rights grounds and its presence on Friday signalled a renewed will on the part of the EU to make the secular state feel part of the European picture.
